2054.note: Only XLVII 114 (19 May 1778, to 'Benson', i.e. Bancroft) is marked 'In cipher', and the APS's own Calendar (Hays 1908) summarises its whole content (Williams's charge, Wharton's denial), so it was read at least in substance; XLVII 115 (to Williams, 20 May) carries no cipher mark.

seen.extent: Mss.B.F85 vol. XLVII, 114 (2 p.) and 115 (2 p.); one letter in cipher at most.
seen.cipher: Hays, Calendar IV (APS): 'From Samuel Wharton to Benson [Paris]. 1778. May 19. Mr. [John] Williams charges him with having carried the letter he gave him directed to Dr. Franklin, to Lord North ... L. (In cipher.) 2 p. XLVII, 114.' Footnote: 'Name under which Silas Deane received letters from England.' Next entry: 'From Samuel Wharton to John Williams, Downing St., London. 1778. May 20. ... L. S. 2 p. (In duplicate.) XLVII, 115.' with no cipher mark. The calendar paraphrases the content of 114 in full, so a reading existed by 1908; whether an interlinear or a key sits on the leaf is unseen. Lead corrections: the 19 May letter is addressed to 'Benson' (identified by the Franklin Papers editors as Bancroft, against Hays's Deane), and only it is in cipher.
